fr.elements: Main Building; Front Driveway; Access Road; Landscaped Area; Open Green Space; Perimeter Fencing; Street Frontage; Open Terrain; Unpaved Circulation Route; Vegetation Overhang
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Open Terrain; Limited Rear Access; Dense Vegetation
fr.recommendations: Confirming address numbers are clearly visible from the street and at the driveway entrance could significantly improve response times given the single access point and extended driveway length. Ensuring the driveway and unpaved circulation route remain clear of obstructions wide enough to accommodate emergency apparatus would support effective access and turnaround capability. Where vegetation overhangs the driveway corridor, maintaining adequate vertical clearance could facilitate unimpeded apparatus travel. Identifying and communicating an alternate staging area within the open terrain to responding units may assist operations should the primary access point become blocked during an incident.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Brush Concentration; Scattered Shrubs; Vegetation Adjacent to Structure; Limited Defensible Space; Brushland Interface; Scattered Shrubs; Single Access Route; Long Driveway; Open Terrain; Fuel Continuity; Mixed Vegetation Cover
wildfire.recommendations: Reducing the concentration of brush and shrubs in the area immediately surrounding the structure would improve defensible space and may reduce fuel continuity across the property. Where shrubs and mixed vegetation are adjacent to the structure, increasing the separation between that vegetation and the building could reduce direct fuel exposure to the structure. Managing scattered shrubs throughout the property to create greater spacing between individual plants may interrupt continuous pathways that could otherwise carry fire toward improvements. Keeping the long driveway clear of encroaching vegetation along its edges would support firefighter access and improve the ability of emergency vehicles to safely reach and exit the property. Because a single access route serves the property, maintaining that route in passable condition at all times is a practical priority for both evacuation and suppression operations. Continued attention to vegetation management near structures and along access routes would support long-term wildfire resilience across the property.
